mentions.name: Red Grid MGRS
mentions.description: A phone app that provides core military land navigation capabilities: live 10-digit MGRS grid, dead reckoning, two-point resection, pace count, back azimuth, magnetic declination (auto or manual), waypoint lists with bearing/distance and a wayfinder arrow, six radio report templates (SALUTE, 9-Line MEDEVAC, SPOT, CASEVAC, ICS 201, CFF), NATO phonetic voice readout, and an NVG-compatible green theme. It runs fully offline with zero tracking, network calls, or data collection, is available on the App Store, and is open source on GitHub.
mentions.problem: The DAGR (AN/PSN-13) military GPS receiver costs $2,500, weighs a pound, and has a dated UI from 2003, so users often end up fighting the device instead of navigating; the military is full of overpriced, outdated systems that a modern phone could handle better.
mentions.audience: Soldiers and military personnel who need land navigation, patrol planning, grid reporting, and field radio reports — the app's stated military users are outside the available audience enum, so no label is proposed.
mentions.source_excerpt: I built Red Grid MGRS to put the same core land nav capabilities into a phone app.
